title: Why melting ice stays at 0 °C until it has all melted
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: Why doesn't ice get warmer while it melts?
Where does the heat go when ice melts?
Why does a drink with ice stay cold?

explain.say: In ice, water molecules are locked in a regular pattern, only able to vibrate in place. Heat makes them vibrate harder and harder.

draw.text: Why melting ice stays at 0 °C until it has all melted

explain.say: At 0 degrees Celsius the molecules start to break free. All the heat going in is now used to break the bonds holding them in place, not to make them faster, so the temperature stays at 0.
Only when the last bit of ice has melted does the heat start warming the water again. Melting a gram of ice takes 334 joules, enough to warm that water by 80 degrees.
So ice at 0 degrees and water at 0 degrees are the same temperature, but the water holds much more energy. That is why ice keeps drinks so cold.

faq.q: Why doesn't ice get warmer while it melts?
faq.a: While it melts, all the heat going in is used to break the bonds between water molecules. None is left to make them move faster, so the temperature stays at 0 degrees until it has all melted.
asks: Why does the temperature stop rising when ice melts?

faq.q: What is latent heat of melting?
faq.a: It is the energy needed to melt a solid without changing its temperature. For ice it is 334 joules for every gram.
asks: What is latent heat of fusion?

faq.q: Why do ice packs keep food cold so well?
faq.a: Melting ice soaks up a lot of heat while staying at 0 degrees, so it holds food near freezing for hours.
asks: Why use ice in a cool box?

faq.q: Why does a drink with ice stay at about 0 °C?
faq.a: As long as there is ice in it, any heat that leaks in goes into melting the ice rather than warming the drink, so it stays close to 0 degrees.
asks: Why do iced drinks stay cold?

faq.a: Attractions between water molecules called hydrogen bonds hold them in a rigid pattern. Melting breaks enough of those bonds for the molecules to slide around.

facts: Melting 1 gram of ice takes 334 joules, enough to heat that gram of water by about 80 degrees Celsius.
A well-stirred mix of ice and pure water stays at 0 degrees Celsius as long as both are present.

quiz.say: While an ice cube is melting, where does the heat it absorbs go?
quiz.show: While an ice cube is melting, where does the heat it absorbs go?

options.show: Into breaking the bonds between molecules
options.say: Into breaking the bonds between molecules

quiz.why: At the melting point the heat is used to free molecules from their fixed pattern, so the temperature stays at 0 degrees.

wrong.0: Energy is never lost; it is stored in the water as latent heat.
wrong.2: The temperature stays at 0 degrees until all the ice has melted.
